product_software_factory_what.message: Builds one graph from your code & documents, lets AI agents work on it, & checks their changes with formal verification.
product_software_factory_what.description: What the Software Factory does, one sentence. Also its link-preview title and meta description.

product_software_factory_audience.message: For software teams that use AI to write code & must stand behind it, starting with startups & small IT companies.
product_software_factory_audience.description: Who the Software Factory is for, one sentence.

product_software_factory_how_1.message: The Software Factory reads your code & its documents into one graph: requirements, design, tests, bug reports & analysis results, each linked to the code it concerns. The graph builds on the <cpg>code property graph</cpg>, which joins the syntax, control flow & data flow of a program. You see it as architecture maps in the <c4>C4 model</c4>, from the whole system down to single functions.
product_software_factory_how_1.description: Software Factory page, 'How it works', paragraph 1 of 3: the graph and the maps. Each tag cites a source: keep it around the words that name the work it cites.

product_software_factory_how_2.message: On top of the graph, AI agents work in steps modelled on <iso-15288>ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288</iso-15288>, the standard for system life cycle processes. A language model writes only what a proof can check: function bodies, against specifications that people approve. Skeletons, tests & documents come from the graph without a model, the same way every time.
product_software_factory_how_2.description: Software Factory page, 'How it works', paragraph 2 of 3: the agent process, and what a language model may write. The tag cites the standard.

product_software_factory_how_3.message: Formal verification checks each function against its specification, with the <prusti>Prusti</prusti> & <verus>Verus</verus> verifiers. When a proof or a test fails, the counterexample goes back to the model, until both pass or a person takes over. Every step leaves an audit trail.
product_software_factory_how_3.description: Software Factory page, 'How it works', paragraph 3 of 3: verification and the repair loop. Prusti and Verus are tool names; each tag cites the paper on the tool.

product_software_factory_state_1.message: It reads Rust, C & TypeScript. On {date, date, long}, it read its own code, {ownFiles, number} Rust files, into a graph of {ownNodes, number} nodes in {ownSeconds, number} seconds, & the {otherFiles, number} files of <ripgrep>ripgrep</ripgrep> into {otherNodes, number} nodes in {otherSeconds, number} seconds. Repeated runs on the same code gave the same result.
product_software_factory_state_1.description: Software Factory page, 'Where it stands', paragraph 1 of 5: a measurement. {date} is the day it was taken; the other placeholders are counts and seconds. ripgrep is the name of an open-source program; the tag cites it.

product_software_factory_state_2.message: Verification runs end to end with Prusti & Verus, so far on small programs such as a ring buffer & the alarm logic of a smoke detector.
product_software_factory_state_2.description: Software Factory page, 'Where it stands', paragraph 2 of 5: what verification covers today.

product_software_factory_state_3.message: For an audit, it exports a traceability matrix & a safety case in the <gsn>Goal Structuring Notation</gsn>. It issues a certificate only when the verifiers ran, every proof obligation holds, every test passes & every requirement is traced.
product_software_factory_state_3.description: Software Factory page, 'Where it stands', paragraph 3 of 5: what it gives auditors. The Goal Structuring Notation is the name of a standard; the tag cites it.

product_software_factory_state_4.message: It reads & writes requirements in the form of <ieee-830>IEEE 830</ieee-830> & design descriptions in the form of <ieee-1016>IEEE 1016</ieee-1016>, & draws UML, SysML & Mermaid diagrams from the code.
product_software_factory_state_4.description: Software Factory page, 'Where it stands', paragraph 4 of 5: the documents it reads and writes. Each tag cites a standard.

product_software_factory_state_5.message: Next, we build the agent process on top of it.
product_software_factory_state_5.description: Software Factory page, 'Where it stands', paragraph 5 of 5: what comes next.

product_erp_crm_what.message: Customers, sales, accounting & HR in one open-data system, with an AI assistant that works on the same data.
product_erp_crm_what.description: What the ERP & CRM does, one sentence. Also its link-preview title and meta description.

product_erp_crm_audience.message: For small businesses that still run on paper & spreadsheets.
product_erp_crm_audience.description: Who the ERP & CRM is for, one sentence.

product_erp_crm_how_1.message: An ERP & CRM built on <twenty>Twenty</twenty>, the open-source CRM, which we extend with accounting, tax, purchasing, sales, payments, inventory & HR.
product_erp_crm_how_1.description: ERP & CRM page, 'How it works', paragraph 1 of 4: what it is built on. Twenty is a product name; the tag cites its source code.

product_erp_crm_how_2.message: Each customer gets its own installation, & all data stays in open formats in one place. An AI assistant works on the same data as your team: it can keep records in order, prepare analyses & draft documents.
product_erp_crm_how_2.description: ERP & CRM page, 'How it works', paragraph 2 of 4: data ownership and the assistant.

product_erp_crm_how_3.message: The ledger keeps amounts as exact decimals in the minor units of <iso-4217>ISO 4217</iso-4217>, never as floating-point numbers. Both the application & the database enforce the rules of bookkeeping: a posted entry never changes, a correction is a reversal entry, & entry numbers have no gaps.
product_erp_crm_how_3.description: ERP & CRM page, 'How it works', paragraph 3 of 4: how the ledger keeps its books exact. The tag cites the currency standard.

product_erp_crm_how_4.message: The AI assistant reads the books through read-only database roles & cannot post to them. Every approval & every closed period is committed to a versioned archive, so each figure can be traced to who approved it & when.
product_erp_crm_how_4.description: ERP & CRM page, 'How it works', paragraph 4 of 4: what the assistant may do, and the audit trail.

product_erp_crm_state_1.message: The specification has about {requirements, number} requirements in {modules, number} modules, written to <iso-29148>ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148</iso-29148>. About a quarter of them are built: the ledger & its rules, the installation per customer, the versioned archive & the assistant’s read-only access.
product_erp_crm_state_1.description: ERP & CRM page, 'Where it stands', paragraph 1 of 2: how much is built. {requirements} and {modules} are counts. The tag cites the standard for requirements.

product_erp_crm_state_2.message: Reports, tax returns & bank reconciliation are not built yet. Our own company is its first user.
product_erp_crm_state_2.description: ERP & CRM page, 'Where it stands', paragraph 2 of 2: what is missing, and who uses it.
